checks.notes:
All three listed documents open locally and I read them in this session. No composition or physical values exist for LuSIC-1 in any of them. R073 lists the methods used (XRD, Raman, μ-EDXRF, bulk and absolute density, cohesion, internal friction angle, particle size, angularity, grain-size curve, PCA against Apollo samples) but reports no numbers, so composition_status 'not_extracted' is correct and there are no new_values.

Feedstock, for notes only: R073 p.1 says 'original raw material was obtained from Tajogaite volcano (La Palma Island)', and that the raw material contained soluble salts, removed by 'two leaching processes for granular materials (CEN/TS 14429 and ultrasound energy)'. It also says LuSIC-1 was refined 'by adjusting its mineralogical composition'. Any data for the raw Tajogaite material would therefore not describe the finished product.

What the extractor missed: R074's germination findings (toxic elements such as aluminium, nutritional deficiencies, very fine dusty particles, compaction) come from tests in a different simulant: 'germination experiments were tested in other lunar simulant LZS-1 (developed at IGEO in 2022)'. None of these may be attributed to LuSIC-1.

Library sweep: grep -rliw 'LuSIC-1' over Sources_text finds only the three listed documents. The unhyphenated 'LuSIC1' finds nothing. A broader search for 'lusic|ibea-carabela|tajogaite' adds only CPESS-8_2025_Alberquilla_PT_PaLMALab_abstract.pdf, which matches through 'Tajogaite' and does not name LuSIC-1. CPESS-8_2025_Programa.pdf lists only the Alberquilla PaLMALab talk, not LuSIC-1. No other document in the library names the product.

The ADS URLs for R073/R074 return HTTP 405 and scixplorer.org returned an empty 202, so both citations rest on the matching local PDFs. The captures a previous agent left in the shared scratchpad (aviaciondigital Green Moon article, ufofeed Hispansion/Terralun article) do not name LuSIC-1. Terralun is a different product and must not be linked to it.

Scope: both abstracts describe LuSIC-1 as a lunar simulant targeting Apollo 17, so it is in scope. The PAMMAT funding covers Mars and Moon work, but that does not change the product's lunar designation.
